answers.c_hidden_obligation: YES. `EVP_DigestInit_ex` sets `(*ctx).digest = type_` at src/evp/digest.rs:2311 and only then calls the fallible `newctx` (:2328); when newctx answers NULL the failure return at :2332 leaves digest!=NULL with algctx==NULL (:2335 sets algctx only on success). EVP_MD_CTX_copy_ex classifies on `in->digest != NULL` (:2981) and so runs the copyctx arm, passing that NULL at :3042/:3079. A legitimate C sequence (failed init, then copy of/onto a same-method context) therefore calls `ptr::copy` of size_of::<ShaCtx>() >= 1 through NULL. findings.statement: src/evp/digest.rs:3042 and :3079 call the provider `copyctx` with `(*out).algctx` / `(*in_).algctx` untested for NULL. The state is reachable: :2311 sets `digest = type_`, :2328 calls the fallible newctx, :2332 returns on failure leaving algctx NULL (:2335 sets it only on success). The same function's re-acquiring arm guards exactly this at :3131, which is the crate's own evidence that NULL is possible. `ptr::copy` of size_of::<T>() through NULL is UB. Not reachable from safe Rust (the entry point is `pub unsafe extern "C"`), but it is a C-valid sequence; §17/§21.1 require the fault not be reproduced undocumented. No copyctx divergence entry exists.

The five hand-written `copyctx` definitions (digest.rs:658, 970, 1165, 1348, 1898) have no `# Safety` fn contract, while the sibling macro copyctx at :447-449 does. The v1i receipt records a contract for the site, but the interface carries none: a documentation-only discharge for an operation whose precondition the caller does not establish.

For OSSH-V1I-059/060/061/064 the receipt's `established_by` says 'caller: ctx_set1_dup! passes the owned incumbent member to this thunk'. These four thunks are never passed to ctx_set1_dup!; they are used only as `Some(<thunk>)` arguments to OPENSSL_sk_pop_free at cmp_ctx.rs:495/496/497/503. The generic contract class absorbed unrelated callbacks; the real per-call-site witness (stack ownership, written by a different function) is absent.
0 of 19 reviewed definitions carries a `# Safety` fn contract; the receipt's contract field is the only contract. For 12 of 19 the in-source comment is circular ('per this function's contract').

The v1i receipt is bound to S'=876900e47b25c01899a2aca97004a77ab60d597f (2026-10-27), an ANCESTOR of the frozen candidate S=0238c6e4adbc7ed85a42be68b6fb965e139bd93e; its declared src_content 8d746bc7... differs from S's 66c1e9ae.... The per-file blobs are stale for exactly the moved files: src/cmp/cmp_ctx.rs (receipt 0b59b0cb..., current c4429e7e...) and src/cmp/cmp_asn.rs (4883b656... vs 8d54b311...); src/provider/digest.rs matches (2affef41...). The 19 operation spans nevertheless hash-match at S (SPAN19 19/19), so only the operation text is content-bound.

8 of the 19 receipt boundary coordinates are stale: itav_free 1697->1706 (+9), rootcakeyupdate_free 1709->1722 (+13), general_name_free_void 392->376 (-16), x509_extension_free_void 396->380 (-16), utf8_string_free_void 400->384 (-16), itav_free_void 408->388 (-20), policy_free_void 412->392 (-20), cmp_ctx_set_md 427->407 (-20). cmp_ctx_set_md's caller citations are stale by 20 (578/587/1588/1593 vs 558/567/1568/1573).

8 of the 19 closure rows have covers_site=false yet content_address_accepts=true and are carried as discharged (e.g. OSSH-V1I-067: declared 1697, current 1706, covers_current_coordinate=false). Content binding is sound, but the declared coordinate does not identify the site; this is the known b75 defect class recurring in v1i.

Disposition citations that cannot resolve to a site or a contract: for this batch OSSH-V1I-060 cites cmp_ctx.rs:396 (blank) and OSSH-V1I-069 cites cmp_asn.rs:1709 (the closing brace of itav_free); receipt-wide CLOC19 reports 8 such rows (060,062,069,072,074,077,079,080).

The inventory records `actual_definition_line: 449` for all five `copyctx` obligations, which is the macro copyctx at provider/digest.rs:449, not the reviewed item at 658/970/1165/1348/1898; the `resolution: qualified` binding is therefore mis-resolved even though the recorded line does hold the item.
